title: The sage who fell from the sky
translation: Nothing throws people off like lust. We really are fools. Take perfume: you know perfectly well someone just put it on their clothes, it's not even theirs, and still, when it smells good, your heart skips a beat.

The sage of Kume could fly, until he saw the white legs of a woman doing the washing and lost his powers. I believe it. Skin is different. Fair, smooth, soft arms and legs aren't something you put on. They're the real thing. No wonder he fell.
original: {世|よ}の{人|ひと}の{心|こころ}を{惑|まど}はすこと{色欲|しきよく}には{如|し}かず。
{人|ひと}の{心|こころ}は{愚|おろ}かなるものかな。
{匂|にほ}ひなどは{仮|かり}のものなるに、しばらく{衣裳|いしやう}に{薫物|たきもの}すと{知|し}りながら、えならぬ{匂|にほ}ひには、{必|かなら}ず{心|こころ}ときめきするものなり。
{久米|くめ}の{仙人|やまびと}の、{物|もの}{洗|あら}ふ{女|をんな}の{脛|はぎ}の{白|しろ}きを{見|み}て、{通|つう}を{失|うしな}ひけむは、まことに{手足|てあし}{膚|はだへ}などのきよらに、{肥|こ}え{膏|あぶら}づきたらむは、{外|ほか}の{色|いろ}ならねばさもあらむかし。
literal: Nothing equals lust in leading astray the hearts of people in the world.
The human heart is a foolish thing.
Scent and the like is a temporary thing, and though one knows that (someone) has for a while perfumed their clothes with incense, at an exquisite scent one's heart always flutters.

That the sage of Kume, seeing the whiteness of the shins of a woman washing things, lost his powers: truly, when hands, feet and skin are fair, plump and glossy, since that is not a colour from outside, it may well be so.

notes.text: {如|し}かず: 'nothing equals'. {色欲|しきよく}: sexual desire, a Buddhist term. Kenkō writes this as a priest, and he means it as a warning.
Heian and Kamakura nobles burned incense ({薫物|たきもの}) under their clothes so the scent stayed in the fabric. Each person had a personal blend, and people recognised each other by it.
ときめく: 'to flutter, to beat fast'. Modern ときめき, the word for that feeling, is the same.

The sage of Kume, a legend from older story collections: a hermit who had learned to fly saw a young woman washing clothes in a river, her legs bare, and fell out of the sky. In the story he then married her. 'Lost his powers' means he fell.
The contrast with the incense: a scent is added from outside, it is not the person's own ({仮|かり}のもの), but skin is the real thing. That is the reason he gives for why the sage had no chance.
